title: Commercial Paralegal
description:
Commercial Paralegal - Watford

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Commercial Paralegal with strong contract and document management experience to join a well- known international business in Watford on an initial 6-month contract basis, with a strong likelihood of extension.

As a Commercial Paralegal you will be responsible for reviewing executed contracts, extracting and coding key information and ensuring documents are accurately recoded and uploaded to the relevant systems.

Your skills and experience should include:
- Previous Commercial Paralegal experience
- Strong contract and document management experience
- Excellent attention to detail and organisation
- Experience handling high volumes of documentation

The role is full-time, with the firm looking for someone to work 4 days per week in the Watford office and 1 day from home.

The role is inside IR35, with a day rate of £200-£250 per day ( £52,000-£65,000 annual equivalent).

The ideal start date is October, although November availability may also be considered.

If you are a Commercial Paralegal looking for a new contract opportunity and can commit to 4 days per week in Watford, apply now or get in touch with Alexiane for a confidential conversation.

title: Legal Assistant
description:
Our client is looking for a skilled Private Client Legal Assistant to join their reputable Private Client team. Our distinguished Client offer a salary of up to £32,000pa, generous holiday allowance with option to buy and sell, a health cash plan, death in service cover plus lots more. You'll provide essential secretarial and administrative support to at least two Fee Earners, all while ensuring exceptional service for clients.

Requirements of the Private Client Legal Assistant:
- Have experience in a Private Client Department or relevant legal qualifications
- Secretarial experience in a Law Firm
- Strong communication skills
- Fast and accurate typing, and the ability to multitask, prioritise, and stay calm under pressure

Private Client Legal Assistant - What will be expected of you - a brief overview:
- Follow the Team Leader's guidance to take client instructions and progress matters, including Wills, Powers of Attorney, Estate and Trust administration.
- Ensure all work is prepared accurately and in line with firm standards and TL instructions.
- Manage an assigned caseload, including file management, time recording, accounting and billing.
- Maintain appropriate work-in-progress, manage disbursements, and ensure client money is accurately accounted for and transferred when required.
- Open and close client files, including completing online AML checks.
- Manage Lawyers' diaries and arrange appointments.
- Provide typing and administrative support to fee earners.

Benefits for this Private Client Legal Assistant role:
- Salary up to £32,000pa
- Health cash plan
- Generous holiday allowance with option to buy and sell
- Pension options
- Death in service cover
- Firmwide bonus scheme
- Employee assistance programme

The Firm:
Our client is a distinguished law firm, ranked in the Top 500 and holding numerous prestigious accreditations in recognition of their exceptional legal advice. With a rich history spanning two centuries, they have cultivated a strong and respected presence as a premier law firm in the Hertfordshire and London regions. Committed to progress, they are continually evolving and have a dedicated team of over 100 professionals.

For a more detailed job description for this Private Client Legal Assistant role please contact Mia quoting reference 37094.

title: Paralegal Children's Law
description:
Our award-winning law firm is expanding its specialist Childrens Law department due to continued growth and increasing demand. We are now seeking a dedicated and compassionate experienced Paralegal to join our specialist Children's Law team.

We are proud winners at the Inspiring Hertfordshire Awards 2024 for Diversity & Inclusion and Business of the Year (West Herts), and finalists for Legal Firm of the Year at the British Business Awards 2025. Our work genuinely changes lives, and we are looking for someone who wants their career to do the same.

Job Purpose

As a Paralegal in our Children Department, you ll be part of a passionate and forward-thinking legal team dedicated to supporting families and protecting children s welfare. This is a dynamic and rewarding role where no two days are the same you ll work on a diverse caseload of both private and publicly funded matters, assisting solicitors and counsel in preparing cases, managing client relationships, and ensuring the smooth running of proceedings.

This position offers the opportunity to develop your skills in a supportive environment where learning and growth are encouraged. If you are looking to build on existing experience in Children matters, you ll find a workplace that values compassion, precision, and progress.

Key Responsibilities

Client Work & Case Management

Reporting directly to the Head of Department

Adopting a professional, proactive approach with strong client care skills and a sensitive understanding of clients needs

Assisting with casework across Children matters (both Legal Aid funded and Private Client work)

Undertaking your own advocacy where appropriate

Attending clients, taking detailed instructions, and preparing case files

Managing and responding to correspondence efficiently and professionally

Preparing and managing Legal Aid applications to the Legal Aid Agency

Drafting key legal documents, including C100s, C1 As, witness statements, and processing supporting evidence

Preparing court bundles and instructions to counsel

Conducting legal research to support case strategy and client advice

Attending client conferences

Maintaining accurate time-costing and billing procedures

Implementing any recommendations made during monthly file reviews, ensuring prompt compliance

Ensuring consistent compliance with firm-wide file management and regulatory standards

Delivering high-quality client service in line with the firm s values of empathy, equality, and professionalism

Teamwork & Supervision

Collaborate closely with colleagues and administrative staff to deliver seamless client service

Provide guidance and supervision to colleagues

Participate in team meetings, training, and case discussions

Contribute to creating a positive, supportive, and inclusive team culture

Professional Development & Compliance

Maintain up-to-date knowledge of family and children matter including relevant legislation and case law

Ensure compliance with the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) Code of Conduct and Legal Aid Agency requirements

Engage in supervision and continuous professional development activities

Assist in developing internal best practice standards and contribute to quality assurance processes

Person Specification

Qualifications & Experience

Completed the LPC or commenced the SQE

Hands-on experience in private and/or public children law matters (e.g. Child Arrangements Orders, Prohibited Steps Orders, Specific Issue Orders)

Excellent attention to detail, organisation, and time management skills

A collaborative mindset, bringing positivity and support to the team

Confidence in using IT systems and the Legal Aid Agency s CCMS portal

Skills & Competencies

Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage urgent and sensitive cases

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Ability to work calmly and effectively under pressure

Strong client care and advocacy skills, with a compassionate and professional approach

Ability to meet deadlines and ensure compliance

Attention to detail and ability to work independently as well as collaboratively

Commitment to trauma-informed practice and continuous learning

Desirable

Fluency in additional languages

Experience in community outreach or public engagement

Personal Attributes

Empathetic, approachable, and emotionally intelligent

Professional and composed when managing sensitive and high-stress situations

Proactive, self-motivated, and adaptable

Resilient, with a commitment to providing exceptional service to vulnerable clients

Team-oriented and passionate about supporting others development

title: Property Paralegal
description:
Property Paralegal Residential Conveyancing
Location: St Albans
Job Type: Full-time
Salary: £25,000 £28,000 per annum, depending on experience

Role Overview

An opportunity has arisen for an organised and proactive Property Paralegal to join a busy residential conveyancing team in St Albans. The successful candidate will have a minimum of five years experience in a law firm and will be capable of confidentially assisting with a broad range of residential sales, purchases and post-completion matters, under the supervision of a fee earner.

This role will suit a candidate who is methodical, client-focused and able to manage a varied workload efficiently. The successful applicant should be ready to contribute from the outset and support the team in progressing matters from instruction through to post-completion.

Key Responsibilities

General Conveyancing Support

Assist fee earners with the day-to-day management of residential conveyancing files.

Open new files and carry out initial administrative procedures in accordance with the firm s policies.

Undertake client due diligence, source of funds/source of wealth checks and other compliance procedures as required.

Prepare client care documentation and ensure files are maintained accurately and in good order.

Keep case management systems and internal records fully updated.

Liaise with clients, estate agents, mortgage brokers, lenders, solicitors and management companies in a professional and timely manner.

Monitor key dates, deadlines and undertakings to ensure matters progress efficiently.

Deal with routine telephone and email enquiries and provide regular updates to clients and third parties.

Sales Transactions

With appropriate supervision from a fee earner, the role will include:

Drafting and issuing contract packs.

Obtaining official copies and title documents from HM Land Registry.

Ordering freehold and leasehold management information packs.

Corresponding with landlords, managing agents and management companies.

Requesting redemption statements from lenders.

Reviewing enquiries raised by the buyer s solicitors and preparing draft replies for approval.

Assisting clients in providing information and documents required to respond to enquiries.

Liaising with estate agents and clients regarding transaction progress.

Preparing transfer documentation for approval.

Assisting with exchange of contracts.

Attending to completion and dealing with associated administrative steps.

Assisting with the discharge of mortgages and other sale-related formalities.

Purchase Transactions

With appropriate supervision from a fee earner, the role will include:

Ordering conveyancing searches and monitoring results.

Reviewing search result and reporting relevant issues to the fee earner.

Reviewing mortgage offers and identifying key conditions for the fee earner s attention.

Reviewing replies to enquiries and supporting the fee earner in raising any follow-up enquiries.

Liaising with clients, estate agents, lenders and brokers regarding transaction progress.

Drafting transfer deeds and other ancillary conveyancing documents.

Drafting deeds of covenant, notices and other leasehold documentation where required.

Preparing draft property reports and title documentation for approval by the fee earner.

The preparation and drafting completion statements.

Carrying out pre-exchange and pre-completion searches, including priority and bankruptcy searches.

Assisting with exchange of contracts.

Preparing and submitting certificates of title to lenders, where appropriate.

Assisting with completion, including requesting mortgage funds and preparing completion packs.

Coordinating completion arrangements with all parties and ensuring funds are dealt with promptly and accurately.

Preparation and drafting of completion statements.

Post-Completion Matters

Drafting and submitting SDLT returns within the relevant time limits.

Preparing and submitting AP1 applications.

Preparing and submitting first registration applications.

Drafting RX forms and other Land Registry forms as required.

Dealing with straightforward HM Land Registry requisitions.

Serving notices on landlords and management companies where required.

Updating lender portals and attending to post-completion lender requirements.

Ensuring completed registration documents are sent to clients and lenders as appropriate.

Closing files in accordance with firm procedures, including archiving and final file checks.

Candidate Requirements

A minimum of two years experience working in a law firm.

Previous experience handling residential conveyancing matters, including both sales and purchases.

Good working knowledge of the conveyancing process from instruction to post-completion.

Experience of dealing with leasehold transactions would be advantageous.

Familiarity with HM Land Registry procedures and SDLT requirements.

Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

A high level of accuracy and attention to detail.

A professional and client-focused approach.

Confidence in working both independently and as part of a team.

Competence in using case management systems and standard Microsoft Office applications.

Desirable Skills and Experience

Experience of dealing with management companies and leasehold property transactions.

Experience of preparing first registration applications.

Familiarity with lender portals and mortgage lender requirements.

Previous experience of handling straightforward Land Registry requisitions.

An understanding of law firm compliance procedures, including anti-money laundering requirements.

Personal Attributes

Exceptionally organised and methodical.

Able to work calmly under pressure and to tight deadlines.

Proactive and willing to take ownership of tasks.

Reliable, adaptable and commercially aware.

Committed to providing a high standard of client service.

Summary

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Property Paralegal seeking a full-time role within a residential conveyancing team in St Albans. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting fee earners across a varied caseload and ensuring transactions progress smoothly and efficiently.
